title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Sunsets Warning Praise And Servanthood While Standing

questions.question: What time of day is described in this passage?
questions.answer: Sunset, the time of Maghrib.

questions.question: What season change does sunset make a person think about?
questions.answer: It makes a person think about winter beginning after summer and autumn.

questions.question: What happens to the beautiful living things mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They pass away and disappear.

questions.question: What personal event in human life does this time also remind a person of?
questions.answer: It reminds a person of death and entering the grave.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to the people of the world when this world comes to its end?
questions.answer: They move on to other worlds.

questions.question: What image is used to show that the world’s testing time will end?
questions.answer: The passage describes its light being put out.

questions.question: What warning does sunset give to people who are attached only to temporary things?
questions.answer: It warns them not to treat passing things as if they will last forever.

questions.question: Why is the warning called serious or strong?
questions.answer: Because it reminds people that beauty, life, and the world itself do not stay.

questions.question: How does the passage make sunset feel: cheerful, ordinary, or solemn? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: Solemn, because it brings thoughts of loss, death, and the ending of the world.

questions.question: What prayer time is the target passage about?
questions.answer: The Maghrib time at sunset.

questions.question: What happens to the lovely things from warm seasons when winter begins?
questions.answer: They disappear and are left behind.

questions.question: How does the passage connect sunset with people’s loved ones?
questions.answer: It says death separates a person from the people he loves.

questions.question: Where does the passage say a person goes after death?
questions.answer: Into the grave.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to the world itself one day?
questions.answer: It will die and come to an end.

questions.question: When the world ends, where do its inhabitants go?
questions.answer: They go to other worlds.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about worldly things that people love too much?
questions.answer: They are short-lived and cannot stay forever.

questions.question: Give one feeling the passage may create in a careful reader.
questions.answer: It may create seriousness, reflection, or sadness.

questions.question: What natural moment begins the ideas in this passage?
questions.answer: The setting of the sun.

questions.question: What happens to the fine things of summer and autumn in the passage’s picture?
questions.answer: They vanish as winter begins.

questions.question: What human experience is compared to that leaving behind of beautiful things?
questions.answer: A person’s death.

questions.question: What is left behind when a person dies, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The people he loves.

questions.question: What place is mentioned as the next stage after death?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: Besides individual death, what much bigger ending does the passage mention?
questions.answer: The end of the whole world.

questions.question: What happens to the world’s people at that great ending?
questions.answer: They are transferred to other worlds.

questions.question: What does the ending of the world show about this world?
questions.answer: It shows this world is temporary and not permanent.

questions.question: Who especially receives a warning in the passage?
questions.answer: People who love passing things as if they were permanent.

questions.question: What is the central message of the whole passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: Sunset teaches that everything in this world passes away, so people should not cling to temporary things.

questions.question: Which prayer time is linked here with endings and departures?
questions.answer: Maghrib, the prayer at sunset.

questions.question: What happens at the start of winter that helps explain the meaning of sunset?
questions.answer: The gentle and beautiful things of the warmer seasons fade away.

questions.question: What does this fading away help a person remember about his own life?
questions.answer: That he too will die and leave this world.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does death affect a person’s relationship with loved ones?
questions.answer: It causes a sorrowful separation from them.

questions.question: What destination is mentioned after this separation?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: What future event for the whole world is described in a dramatic way?
questions.answer: The world’s final end.

questions.question: What symbol in the passage suggests that the world’s test period will be over?
questions.answer: Its lamp being extinguished.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest is wrong with loving temporary things too deeply?
questions.answer: It leads a person to depend on things that will disappear.

questions.question: What part of the day does the passage focus on?
questions.answer: The time when the sun goes down.

questions.question: What change in nature is used first to teach a lesson?
questions.answer: The move from the beauty of summer and autumn to winter.

questions.question: In that picture from nature, what happens to lovely creatures?
questions.answer: They disappear.

questions.question: What sad event in a person’s life does the passage say sunset can bring to mind?
questions.answer: A person’s death.

questions.question: After that event, what separation takes place?
questions.answer: He parts from those he loves.

questions.question: What place does the passage mention after this worldly departure?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: What larger departure is mentioned for all living people when the world ends?
questions.answer: They leave this world and go to other worlds.

questions.question: What object is described as being put out when the world’s trial ends?
questions.answer: A lamp.

questions.question: If someone treats temporary things like they are everlasting, how does the passage respond to that?
questions.answer: It gives that person a strong warning.

questions.question: What prayer time is being described through images of fading light and endings?
questions.answer: Maghrib time.

questions.question: What happens to the beauties of the warmer seasons when winter starts?
questions.answer: They are gone and leave with sadness.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention sad goodbyes?
questions.answer: To show that many things in this life do not remain.

questions.question: What does sunset remind a person about his own future?
questions.answer: That he will die one day.

questions.question: According to the passage, what must a dying person leave behind?
questions.answer: The people he loves.

questions.question: What place is named as part of what comes after death?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: What final event for the whole world is also brought to mind at sunset?
questions.answer: The death and ending of the world.

questions.question: What happens to the world’s inhabitants after that ending?
questions.answer: They pass on to other worlds.

questions.question: What truth about worldly beloved things is taught by this passage?
questions.answer: They are passing and cannot remain forever.
